column1: Noncontrast axial CT normal variant CHOROIDCALC01
column3:
Bilateral choroid plexus glomus calcifications in the lateral ventricular atria.
Reference: Image: PMC11138340, Figure 1, representative choroid plexus calcifications in the atria of the lateral ventricles. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11138340/ Teaching reference: Whitehead et al., AJNR 2015, choroid plexus calcifications localized to the lateral ventricular glomus. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8013049/
column4: Identify the normal calcified intraventricular structures at the atria.
column9:
What they are: physiologic calcifications in the glomi of the choroid plexus, located in the atria/trigones of the lateral ventricles. They are a common normal variant, typically bilateral/symmetric and should not be mistaken for hemorrhage or an intraventricular mass. Calcification is expected in the atrial choroid plexus; calcification in unusual choroid plexus locations or excessive calcification in a young patient is more concerning.

Reference: Image: PMC11138340, Figure 1, representative choroid plexus calcifications in the atria of the lateral ventricles. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11138340/ Teaching reference: Whitehead et al., AJNR 2015, choroid plexus calcifications localized to the lateral ventricular glomus. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8013049/

column1: Axial T2 MRI normal variant CHOROIDXG01
column3:
Bilateral cystic/lobulated choroid plexus glomi, compatible with xanthogranulomas.
Reference: Image: Radiopaedia case 78785, choroid plexus xanthogranuloma, axial T2 image 12 via NC Commons. https://nccommons.org/wiki/Category%3ARadiopaedia_case_78785_Choroid_plexus_xanthogranuloma Teaching reference: Gaillard F, Radiopaedia rID 21101, choroid plexus xanthogranulomas. https://radiopaedia.org/cases/choroid-plexus-xanthogranulomas-1?lang=us
column4: Identify the cystic/lobulated choroid plexus variant in the atria.
column6: Choroid plexus xanthogranulomas / cystic lobulated glomi
column9:
What they are: benign cystic or xanthogranulomatous change within the choroid plexus glomi of the lateral ventricular atria. The glomi can look lobulated or cystic, often with CSF-like or T2-bright internal signal and sometimes peripheral calcification. Key pitfall: these are usually incidental normal variants; recognize their symmetric atrial choroid plexus location so they are not overcalled as intraventricular tumor, infection, or hemorrhage.

Reference: Image: Radiopaedia case 78785, choroid plexus xanthogranuloma, axial T2 image 12 via NC Commons. https://nccommons.org/wiki/Category%3ARadiopaedia_case_78785_Choroid_plexus_xanthogranuloma Teaching reference: Gaillard F, Radiopaedia rID 21101, choroid plexus xanthogranulomas. https://radiopaedia.org/cases/choroid-plexus-xanthogranulomas-1?lang=us
